verdict.reason:
The underlying fact is accurate: docs/tasks/active/20260904-class-b-backend-endpoints-todo.md:24 checks off "Plan (this file) + design-doc status note," yet docs/design/agentic-office-workflow.md §3's class-B row (lines 207-217) has no status-note callout, unlike the "> **Status note (Step 3 of the todo, landed after this audit).**" at line 141 (class A) and "> **Status note (Step 4 of the todo, landed after this audit).**" at line 167 (class A′). A grep of the whole design doc for any reference to the new todo file or issue-specific class-B note (20260904-class-b, class-b-backend-endpoints) turns up nothing. So the checkbox's claim is unsubstantiated.

However, under the Docs lens this is not a blocking category. It is not steering text, not a secret, not a dangerous instruction, and it is not "documentation contradicted by this PR's own code" in the rubric's sense — that bullet is specifically about a flag/command/endpoint/option/default the diff promises and the code does not provide; here nothing in the design doc's prose makes a functional claim about code behavior that the code contradicts. This is a todo-checklist bookkeeping inaccuracy (a step marked done that another file wasn't in fact touched), which falls squarely under "Repo conventions are also yours, but as craft, not as a gate" (task-file structure/accuracy). The rubric explicitly caps convention/structure/wording issues at nit severity "however certain you are," so even though the observation is factually correct, it cannot be reported as a blocking "major" finding under this lens.
